verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai:
“Tell the Israelites, ‘When you get to the land I’m giving you, give the land a Sabbath for Yahweh.
For six years, plant your fields, trim your vines, and bring in what they produce.
In year seven the land gets a Sabbath of complete rest, a Sabbath for Yahweh. Don’t plant your fields or trim your vines.
Don’t harvest what grows on its own or gather grapes from vines you haven’t trimmed. Give the land a whole year of rest.
What the land produces during its Sabbath will feed you, your male and female servants, your hired workers, and the foreigners living with you.
Everything the land produces will also feed your livestock and the animals in your land.
“‘Count off seven Sabbath years, seven times seven years. That adds up to forty-nine years.
On day ten of the seventh month, the Day of Atonement, blast the trumpet so it sounds throughout your land. 📯
Set apart year fifty as holy and announce freedom to everyone living in the land. It’s your Jubilee. Each of you will go back to your own property and your family.
The fiftieth year is your Jubilee. Don’t plant crops that year, harvest what grows on its own, or gather grapes from vines you haven’t trimmed.
It’s the Jubilee, and it’s holy to you. Eat what the field produces right out of the field.
“‘In the Year of Jubilee, each of you will go back to your own property.
“‘When you sell something to your neighbor or buy something from them, don’t cheat each other.
Set the purchase price by how many years have passed since the Jubilee. Your neighbor is selling you the harvests for the years that remain.
If there are lots of years left, the price goes up. If there are only a few, the price goes down. What you’re paying for is the number of harvests.
Don’t cheat one another. Show reverence for your God, because I’m Yahweh your God.
“‘Keep my laws and follow my instructions, and you’ll live safely in the land.
The land will produce its crops, you’ll have enough to eat your fill, and you’ll live there safely.
You might ask, “What will we eat in year seven if we can’t plant anything or bring in a harvest?”
I’ll send my blessing on you in year six, so the land will grow enough food for three years.
You’ll plant in year eight and keep eating from what you stored up until year nine. Eat from those supplies until the new harvest comes in.
“‘Don’t sell the land away for good. The land is mine, and you live with me as foreigners and guests.
Wherever you own land, you must allow it to be bought back.
“‘If one of your people falls into poverty and sells some of their property, their closest relative can come and buy back what they sold.
If they have nobody to buy it back but they get back on their feet and come up with enough money,
they’ll work out how many years have passed since the sale, pay the buyer back for the years still left, and return to their property.
If they can’t buy it back, it stays with the buyer until the Year of Jubilee. In the Jubilee the property goes free, and the original owner returns to it.
“‘If someone sells a home in a walled city, they have one year from the sale to buy it back. That right lasts a full year.
If the house isn’t bought back within that year, it belongs to the buyer and their descendants in perpetuity. It won’t go back in the Jubilee.
Houses in villages without walls count as open farmland. They can be bought back, and they’ll go back to the original owners in the Jubilee.
“‘The Levites can buy back homes in the cities they own at any time.
A Levite can buy back a house sold in one of their cities. It’ll be released in the Jubilee, because the houses in the Levites’ cities are their property among the Israelites.
The pasturelands around their cities can’t be sold. Those lands belong to them forever.
“‘If one of your people falls into poverty and can’t keep themselves afloat, help them out so they can live with you like a foreigner or a temporary resident.
Don’t charge them interest or make a profit off them. Show reverence for your God so your neighbor can stay and live among you.
Don’t lend them money at interest or sell them food for a profit.
I’m Yahweh your God. I brought you out of Egypt to give you Canaan and to be your God.
“‘If one of your people falls into poverty and sells themselves to you, don’t make them work as a slave.
They’ll stay with you as a hired worker and temporary resident and work for you until the Year of Jubilee.
Then they’ll leave with their children, return to their family, and go back to their family’s land.
They’re my servants. I brought them out of Egypt. They must not be sold as slaves.
Don’t treat them harshly. Show reverence for your God.
“‘As for male and female slaves, you may buy them from the nations around you.
You may also buy from the children of foreigners living with you and from their families who have had children in your land. They’ll become your property.
You may leave them to your children as an inheritance and hold them as slaves for life. But when it comes to your fellow Israelites, don’t rule harshly over one another.
“‘If a foreigner living among you gets rich while one of your own people falls into poverty and sells themselves to that foreigner or to someone in the foreigner’s family,
they can still be bought back after the sale. One of their brothers can buy them back,
or their uncle, cousin, or any close relative in their family. If they come into enough money, they can buy their own freedom.
They’ll work out the price with the person who bought them. Count the years from the sale to the Jubilee and price those years at the rate of a hired worker.
If lots of years are left, they’ll pay back the share of the original price that covers those years to buy their freedom.
If only a few years are left until the Jubilee, they’ll work out the amount with the buyer and pay the share for the years left to serve.
Treat them like a worker hired year by year. Don’t let the buyer rule over them harshly while you stand by.
If they aren’t bought back in one of these ways, they and their children will go free in the Year of Jubilee.
The Israelites are my servants. I brought them out of Egypt. I’m Yahweh your God.
